text:
ryan: Escalation from ACME via support — they started seeing tool/function calls get suppressed after yesterday's canary rollout (canary-id: can-2026-03-16-42). ~30% of assistant turns that used to call address_lookup now return plain text. Customer supplied request_id 0x9f3a2 and a sample convo. Marking P2 for now, escalate to P1 if we can reproduce.

maria: ping @ashley @lee. Deploy bot shows canary rolled at 2026-03-16T21:05Z, variant=runtime-v3.2.1-bridgeopt. Any known changes to fn-bridge or schema matching? :eyes: 

deploy-bot: Canary rollout can-2026-03-16-42 completed at 2026-03-16T21:05:13Z. Diff: fnbridge schema strictness toggle enabled (default=false -> true for canary).

ashley: I pulled the canary diff — we enabled stricter arg-schema enforcement in the fn-bridge mapper. The intent was to reduce malformed invocations, but this would reject tool calls if the model's args don't strictly match the schema.

ryan: Customer sample payload (redacted):
```json
{
  "input": "Find HQ address for Acme Corp.",
  "tools": [{ "name": "address_lookup", "schema": { "query": "string" } }],
  "model": "redwood-v0.9.3-llm",
  "bridge": "fnbridge-v2"
}
```
And the model output they sent back (what used to happen):
```json
{"tool_call": {"name": "address_lookup", "args": {"query": "Acme HQ"}}}
```
Now they get: "I can't find that" (no tool_call emitted). They also shared raw assistant output which appears to be a JSON-ish blob but the bridge rejected it with: `schema mismatch: field 'query' expected string, got tokenized/object`.

lee: That error aligns with the strictness change. We introduced a small encoder wrapper that returns args as token arrays in edge cases. Previously the bridge coerced to strings. So the bridge sees non-string and drops the invocation.

ashley: Quick repro steps (what I used locally):
1) POST to /v1/chat with the given payload
2) model set to redwood-v0.9.3-llm
3) set header X-Bridge-Variant: fnbridge-v3.2.1-bridgeopt
Expect: tool_call emitted. Actual (canary): text-only response.

ryan: Customer provided a curl repro — pasted (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Request-ID: 0x9f3a2" -d '{"input":"Find HQ address for Acme"}'
```
They said toggling model to older runtime fixed it for them.

maria: Suggestion: 1) rollback fn-bridge strictness on canary -> mitigates customer impact, 2) add tolerant_schema=true for Acme tenant as fast mitigation, 3) run a small eval across recent chat logs to measure % dropped toolcalls. Who can perform rollback?

ashley: I can flip the canary back to relax the schema check (fast rollback toggle). But we should capture a failing request trace first. Ryan — can you grab full request_id and full assistant output from the customer? Need raw assistant content and the bridge rejection logs (trace id will link).

ryan: Requested raw transcript + full headers from ACME. They asked for ETA before rolling back. I told them ~30–60 mins for toggle if needed.

lee: Long term fix: make bridge do a soft-coercion pass for args (strings <- tokens/arrays) and add a regression test for model arg shapes. I'll open a PR to add coercion + unit tests.

ashley: For immediate triage: I'm going to enable tolerant_schema=true for the Acme org on canary nodes (no global rollback) so we can confirm fix without global impact. After that, if metrics show high suppression, we rollback the canary entirely.

maria: I'll run a quick analytics query: count(suppressed_tool_calls) by hour since 2026-03-16T20:00Z for the canary cohort. Putting this on my dashboard now.

ryan: Action items — I'll list and assign: 
- ryan: collect full raw assistant output + headers from ACME (waiting)
- ashley: enable tolerant_schema=true for Acme tenant on canary nodes (in progress)
- lee: start PR for soft-coercion + unit tests (wip)
- maria: metrics query + metrics alert if suppressed rate > 1%

ashley: quick log snippet from canary node (sensitive keys redacted):
```
WARN fnbridge.mapper: rejected invocation request_id=0x9f3a2 cause=schema_mismatch field=query expected=string got=Array(12)
INFO fnbridge.bridge: dropping tool_call for model_output_id=mo-78ef due_to=strict_schema
```
ryan: Customer replied — wants rollback if we can’t confirm within 1 hour. They shared another request_id: 0x9f7d1 where the same behavior occurred.

maria: If rollback needed, we should coordinate with infra for canary -> previous stable (runtime-v3.2.0). @deploy-bot can you queue a canary rollback ticket?

deploy-bot: Created rollback ticket RB-2026-142 and notified infra on-call. ETA for rollback if approved: ~25 minutes.

lee: Logging note — collect a couple of model outputs from both old and new runtimes and diff the tool_call serialization. That will be the evidence for our bugfix PR.

ryan: I'll update the customer thread with our mitigation plan (tolerant toggle first, rollback if still failing). Adding this thread to the ticket RB-2026-142. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ashley: Leaving a reminder — do not enable tolerant_schema globally until we patch coercion. We want a controlled rollback path.

maria: I'll follow up with a short postmortem if suppression rate > threshold.

ryan: (closing loop) ACME confirmed they saw immediate improvement after the tolerant_schema toggle on their tenant. They're monitoring and will report if anything else pops up. Keeping this open until we merge the coercion fix.
